disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is characterized by one or more episodes of at least two weeks of pervasive low mood and/or loss of interest, accompanied by cognitive, physical, and emotional changes such as altered sleep or appetite, low energy, impaired concentration, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, and recurrent thoughts of death. Episodes often cause significant functional impairment in work, relationships, and self-care, and can last months to years if untreated, with many patients experiencing recurrent episodes across the lifespan. MDD is distinguished from normal grief or adjustment reactions by its persistence, severity, and the breadth of associated symptoms, and from bipolar disorders by the absence of any history of manic or hypomanic episodes. Course and prognosis are shaped by biological vulnerability, personality traits, life stressors, and access to social support and treatment.

narrative.stressor: About two years ago, Marilyn accepted additional responsibilities at her suburban secondary school, taking on an advanced STEM track, standardized test prep coordination, and leadership of both the robotics and coding clubs on top of her full teaching load. At the same time, the district rolled out a new data-driven evaluation system that closely scrutinized test scores and required extensive documentation, which clashed with her perfectionistic, competitive streak and led her to spend most evenings and weekends lesson planning and analyzing student data instead of engaging in her usual hobbies, sports league, and family hikes. Over the next 18 months, the constant pressure to maintain measurable results, frequent curriculum changes, and repeated conflicts with administration over resources for her clubs eroded her sense of mastery and made it harder for her to keep up her meticulously organized home routines and budgeting. She ultimately sought psychiatric care after her principal gently suggested she take a personal day when colleagues noticed she was missing deadlines, skipping the softball league, and talking about feeling unable to get excited about teaching or anything else, which alarmed both her husband and department head.
narrative.chief_complaint: I feel like I’ve lost all interest in teaching and the activities I used to enjoy, and I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to.

narrative.stressor: Around a year and a half ago, Mohamad’s father suffered a stroke that left him with significant mobility issues, and as the most organized sibling living nearby, Mohamad became the primary coordinator of his father’s medical appointments, home modifications, and daily care schedule on top of managing multiple construction projects. His routine-driven nature initially helped him juggle the responsibilities, but as his father’s condition plateaued and required ongoing, indefinite support, the constant caregiving decisions, middle-of-the-night phone calls, and financial worries about long-term care steadily eroded the sense of control he relied on in both work and hobbies. Over time he let go of his woodworking projects, stopped attending his fishing club and strength-training sessions, and began spending most of his non-work hours shuttling between job sites and his parents’ house, feeling increasingly trapped by obligations and quietly pulling away from friends and community events. He finally presented for psychiatric evaluation after his wife and a close friend from the chess club confronted him about how exhausted and withdrawn he had become, and he admitted that, for months, he’d been preoccupied with thoughts that his family might be better off without him, which frightened him enough to agree to see a professional.
narrative.chief_complaint: Lately I keep having thoughts that my family would be better off if I weren’t here, and it’s starting to scare me.

narrative.stressor: Approximately nineteen months ago, Even’s youngest child left for college, and within the same year her long-standing hospital department underwent a major restructuring that shifted her to a more administrative, telehealth-heavy role with less direct patient contact. The combination of an increasingly quiet home, fewer day-to-day parental responsibilities, and a workday now dominated by spreadsheets and virtual meetings disrupted the balance she had previously maintained between data-driven advocacy and the face-to-face community engagement that had given her a sense of purpose. Although she tried to fill the gaps with her garden, yoga, and volunteer work at the food pantry, she found herself spending more time alone, ruminating about whether she had "missed" her chance to build a different life and questioning the value of her current contributions. After over a year of this gradual shift, she sought psychiatric care when she realized she was regularly making small but uncharacteristic errors in her case analyses and struggling to focus during telehealth sessions, prompting concern from a colleague who noticed she no longer seemed mentally present in team meetings.
narrative.chief_complaint: I’m having a really hard time concentrating and making decisions at work, even on tasks that used to feel straightforward.
